text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 10.65% over two weeks and stayed roughly flat today, weighed down by collapsing crude oil prices. Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on November 10th—the lowest since August—after President Trump signaled the Iran conflict could end "fairly soon." For a refiner, lower oil prices are a mixed bag: cheaper feedstock to process sounds good, but refiners make money on the *spread* between crude costs and what they sell gasoline and diesel for, and that spread compresses when crude falls sharply without retail fuel prices dropping as quickly.

The broader pressure comes from geopolitical de-escalation removing a key support for energy prices. Over the past week, crude has cratered from $427-level prices early November, and while refineries are running hot at 94.5% capacity and storage levels remain moderate, the dramatic fall in crude—especially crude falling faster than the demand picture changed—leaves refiner margins under pressure until the market finds a new equilibrium.
